title: A finite-entropy separation of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy
coverage: Read all six sections, the full LaTeX (about 1000 lines). Checked each step of the proof chain: (1) the normalizations of chi and chi*, which agree with each other: GUE entropy 1/2 log(2 pi e w) matches chi* of a semicircular of variance w. (2) The free-flow identity chi*(V_{h+t}) - chi*(V_h) = 1/2 int_0^t Phi*: re-derived, sign correct. (3) The Wick-testing lemma: checked the inclusion-exclusion bijection between deleted adjacent pairs and restored pairs, the gap structure under the external arches, and that the Wick polynomials reduce to Chebyshev U_2, U_3, U_4 in one variable. (4) Prop 3.2: the first-block cumulant expansion, the residual R_i, and the identity ||Z_i - v_i xi_i||^2 = v_i^2(||xi_i||^2 - 1/v_i). (5) Lemma 4.1: the Catalan/Mobius bound 32^m and the noncrossing-pairing sparsity count (1+4 sqrt p)^m; 32 sqrt 5 < 128. (6) The geometric series behind (4.1), and K^6 p^{3/2}/(3a^3) < 1/24 at the threshold. (7) The parameters p=2^64, t=2^48: p/(256v) > 128, against about 52 for the net-cost side. (8) Lemma 5.1: the subsequence choice, de Bruijn, entropy concavity, the matrix integration-by-parts normalization, liminf I_d >= Phi* via Lemma 2.2, and Fatou. (9) Section 6: the uniform block witness, the Markov bounds (32t/p, norm bound 1/16), the operator-norm unitary net (1+2/delta)^{2d^2} with delta = 1/(64 sqrt v) and loss sqrt p/8, the chi-squared MGF 2^{q/2} with q <= 2d^2, the binary KL bound alpha log(1/beta) - log 2, and the Gaussian cross-entropy identity giving limsup H_d <= L(h+t) - 2. Not done: no independent numerical simulation, and no line-by-line check of the cited NS theorems beyond what they are standardly known to say.
main_claim: There is a bounded self-adjoint (p+1)-tuple X = C + sqrt(h) S, with C = (free semicirculars B_1..B_p, plus a commuting uniform-atom variable Y), such that -inf < chi(X) <= chi*(X) - 1/2 < inf. This would settle Voiculescu/Guionnet's finite-entropy equality question negatively.
sibling_notes: Family 298 had no prior sibling entries on the board. The paper cites the companion paper 'An isomorphism of the free group factors' only for context in the introduction; the proof does not use it, so there is no circular dependence. The result is significant. Every step I checked holds, but the claim resolves a well-known open problem and still deserves expert scrutiny, especially of Lemma 3.1 (Wick testing) and of whether liminf I_d can be strictly larger than Phi*, which is what the gap mechanism relies on.
